profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer @ Microsoft | AI Integrations, Document Intelligence
profile.summary:
I’m a Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft with a background spanning AI systems, large‑scale distributed architectures, and video streaming/encoding pipelines. I work across Microsoft 365—especially Word—building high‑reliability services, improving developer velocity, and driving clarity in highly ambiguous problem spaces.
My experience includes designing and scaling document‑centric systems, optimizing real‑time media workflows (H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC, VP9), and building distributed processing pipelines with parallelism, workload balancing, and fault‑tolerant execution. I’m passionate about strong architecture, clean abstractions, and leveraging telemetry to drive reliability and performance improvements.
Across all domains—AI, media, or distributed systems—I focus on creating end‑to‑end solutions that scale, mentoring engineers, and helping teams ship with confidence.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer | OfficeAI
positions.description:
Contribute to AI-powered document creation and understanding experiences across Microsoft 365, building capabilities that help users generate, reason over, and interact with Office content more effectively.
Design and deliver document intelligence technologies that improve content understanding, retrieval, grounding, and generation quality across Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and other Office experiences. Partner with engineering and research teams to identify gaps, validate solutions, and improve the reliability and readiness of AI-powered features.
Drive platform investments in OfficeAgent, helping evolve a unified agent framework capable of creating and managing multiple Office document types through a single agent experience. Contributed to onboarding infrastructure, reusable harnesses, and developer tooling that enable additional applications and teams to integrate with the platform more efficiently.
Build shared services, APIs, and engineering frameworks that accelerate experimentation, reduce development friction, and improve developer productivity across AI initiatives. Operate as a senior technical contributor in highly ambiguous spaces, influencing architecture, mentoring engineers, and helping align technical decisions across product and platform teams.
positions.insights: Software Design, AI Agents and +3 skills

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Optimized codec pipelines (H.264/AVC, H.265/HEVC, VP9) and encoding profiles to improve compression efficiency, latency, and QoE across diverse network conditions.
Built and tuned distributed encoding and packaging systems with parallelism, workload balancing, and fault‑tolerant media processing.
Improved end‑to‑end video delivery reliability through telemetry‑driven profiling, network-aware tuning, and performance optimization across ingestion → encoding → packaging → playback.
positions.insights: Video Processing, Live Video Streaming and +5 skills

positions.title: Software Engineer 2
positions.description:
- Owned core components of the Stream video pipeline, including JIT (Just‑In‑Time) FFmpeg encoding, segment transcoding, and HLS/DASH packaging to deliver reliable playback at scale.
- Developed and refined adaptive bitrate (ABR) ladders by introducing content‑aware bitrate selection, reducing segment size and improving startup time and QoE for high‑motion and low‑motion videos alike.
- Investigated and fixed issues in bitrate upsampling, validating FFmpeg behavior and improving alignment between manifest bitrates and transcoded outputs.
- Drove telemetry‑led analysis of segment sizing, playback failures, and transcoder performance to improve reliability and guide platform decisions.
- Acted as a key contributor across MeTA and CoreMedia teams, collaborating with encoding, SPO, and client stakeholders to diagnose issues, refine encoding strategies, and deliver measurable playback improvements.

positions.title: Consulting Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Contributed to the migration of Japan Airlines’ legacy reservation system to the Amadeus Global Distribution System, enabling modern API‑driven integrations for both internal monoliths and external customer systems.
- Designed and developed new reservation APIs supporting flight availability search, special services (SSR) selection, document validation, payment processing, and checkout flows.
- Collaborated with cross‑functional teams to modernize legacy Java services into scalable, API‑based components, improving reliability and easing partner integrations.
- Delivered well‑tested, production‑ready features including backend services, data‑access layers, and workflow logic using Java and MySQL.
- Ensured code quality and deployment readiness through unit testing, integration testing, and reviews using Git and ClearCase version control systems.

projects.title: Pictrel ERDF et GRDF
projects.description:
Pictrel allows managers to organize electricity and gas interventions in optimized rounds to be assigned to technicians. It helps technicians to have a complete day itinerary just by downloading their round.
The round is made with a best route system that will suggest the best order to execute each intervention based on their location, zone, time and traffic.

Responsibilities:
- Technical architecture. 
- Development.
- Code reviewing.
- Tests (Unitary, Integration and functional) 

Work Environment:
Java 7, Flex, Struts, Spring, Hibernate
WebLogic Server, Oracle Database, Apache httpd
Maven, Git + Gerrit, Jenkins, SonarQube, HP Quality Center

projects.title: Photos/Video Editor app - Growth Hacking
projects.description:
As part of the Growth Hacking team of Microsoft's photos team, I led several experiments trying to bring more users or encourage existing users into using high value actions (import, create albums, upload to onedrive, share, etc.). To accomplish that, I was responsible of implementing (C++, C#, XAML) several projects and analyzing them using our existing tools (Cosmos, Kusto). Below are some of the most relevant projects:
- Add means to select one or several media files directly from a windows directory and have options to create a photo video or photo album.
- Add cloud based comment infrastructure to allow experimentation with different media (text, images, videos, etc) to allow experimentation without needing an app update.
- Add XboxLive sources to your photo library. Tasks included: Authentication, syncing and UI changes.

patents.title: Video encoding using deviation-adjusted bitrate parameter
patents.description:
The patent describes a way to determine a content aware bitrate for sessions where it's not possible to pre-transcode all the video before the first playback session. Those sessions are called Just-In-Time and occur when the first user to ever watch the video clicks playback. The main reasons for companies to not pre-transcode videos is cost, as most of their videos might never be watched.

So, if we are in a JIT session, we don't have a lot of time to pick a right number to feed the encoder during transcoding, mainly because there's a user waiting for the playback to start.

Most of the current techniques to find a good bitrate for a video, require a complete read of the video to analyze it and determine the "optimal" bitrate. For our scenario, that was not possible so we had to come up with a different approach.

Our approach can be summarized as follows:
- Detect video formats that contain the metadata needed to quickly calculate a content aware bitrate.
- Read only the section of the file that contains the metadata. We need to be precise to not download too much file.
- Use the metadata from the file to calculate the standard deviation based on average bitrate.
- Adjust the target bitrate based on standard deviation + average bitrate. The importance of standard deviation is that it will give us a sense of bitrate variability in the video. This is important, as for a video with very low variability, the avg bitrate will be just good to use to encode it, but one with high variability will produce quality loss as we will be asking the encoder to reduce drastically the size of the video for some portions of the file.
